solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Detection means plea is changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of the words plea is are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A lawyer's ploy is spotted when the defendant switches plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the letters of PLEA IS; 'means' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An espial is an act of spying or catching sight of something, a literary word for discovery or detection.

clue.text: First wife is concealing two keys

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'First wife is concealing two keys (5)', gives EVE around A and D (two musical keys) but has no definition for EVADE; the fifteensquared blogger and commenters agree it lacks one.
annotationWithheld.clue: First wife is concealing two keys

clue.text: Picnic arranged to entertain posh composer

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within your home, so one piece goes inside the other
arranged means set out in a different order, so the letters of the word picnic are shuffled

parts.note: U is the crossword letter for upper-class, hence posh

explanation.surface: A smart picnic is laid on with an opera composer as the guest of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles PICNIC into PUCCINI's PCCINI shape, and 'to entertain' puts U inside it after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini was the Italian who wrote the operas La Boheme, Tosca and Madama Butterfly.

clue.text: A feature of credit

definitions.meaning: a characteristic quality or trait that something has
the verb sense: to credit something to someone is to put it down to them

explanation.walkthrough: The noun (stress on the first syllable) is a feature; the verb (stress on the second) means to credit or ascribe.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word names a quality or trait; as a verb it means to ascribe a work or result to someone.

clue.text: Caught by traffic light at bend in road

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
amber is the middle signal on a British traffic light

explanation.surface: A driver gets nabbed by a camera at the lights just where the road curves.
explanation.walkthrough: AMBER is the British name for the yellow light between red and green.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the slight curve or arching of a road surface, so a bend across the road's profile.

clue.text: A calm end to our love-affair

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here taken from calm

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Two lovers wish for a peaceful finish to their romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is borrowed from French and means a love affair, often a secret or illicit one.

clue.text: Knapsack, we hear, carried by travellers

definitions.text: Knapsack, we hear, carried by travellers

parts.words: Knapsack, we hear, carried by travellers
parts.note: knapsack said aloud is 'nap sack', a sack for napping in, which travellers carry rolled up

explanation.surface: Hikers take their rucksacks on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue first reads as a plain backpack; 'we hear' turns it into a sack for a nap, which is a sleeping roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroll is bedding rolled up for carrying, the sleeping kit campers and tramps take along.

clue.text: Practical article is manufactured

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up out of raw material, so the letters of article is are worked into a new word

explanation.surface: A factory boss judges an item purely on whether it is made to be useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges ARTICLE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone realistic is sensible and down-to-earth, taking the practical view of what can be done.

clue.text: A course in writing may bring fortune

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other, as the clue says in

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
Ascot is the Berkshire racecourse famous for Royal Ascot

explanation.surface: Taking a writing class could make you rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A course' looks like a class of lessons, but Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascots are charms believed to bring good luck, so they may bring good fortune.

clue.text: Warm drink with a fruity flavour

definitions.meaning: warm in the sense of friendly and hearty
a sweet fruit drink, often diluted, such as lime or elderflower

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means friendly and affectionate; the noun is a sweet concentrated fruit drink, as in lime juice drinks.

clue.text: Sneak into class with a lot of books

parts.note: into gives in, its first part
a form is a school class in Britain
NT is the New Testament, a collection of many books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A tell-tale pupil slips into the classroom carrying a pile of books.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a class or year group is a FORM.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak is someone who tells tales, one who informs on others to those in authority.

clue.text: One with a suit may give tip to Ernie

indicators.note: to give is to bend or yield out of shape, so the letters of tip to Ernie are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler hoping for a win sends a hint to ERNIE, the premium bond machine.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the computer that picks Britain's Premium Bond winners. 'may give' rearranges TIP TO ERNIE. 'Suit' is a lawsuit or plea, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is a formal request or legal action, and the person bringing one is a petitioner.

clue.text: Ring-road, junction and by-pass

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written with letters as MI
a T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles

explanation.surface: A list of road features for a traffic planner: ring road, junction and bypass.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, so MI stands for road. 'by-pass' looks like another road feature but is the verb, to skip.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to skip or leave it out, which is exactly what omitting does.

clue.text: A valediction is something cast in gold

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as in says

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold, from Latin aurum
a die is thrown or cast in dice games

explanation.surface: A farewell speech is engraved in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast in gold' suggests metal-working, but the die is the dice thrown in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French-derived goodbye, and a valediction is a word or speech of farewell.

clue.text: Performed in a group that's dissolute

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as in says

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
done, as in a play that has been done or performed

explanation.surface: A singer who has played with a band is accused of loose living.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned can describe a person who is unrestrained and immoral, given over to vice like a dissolute one.

clue.text: Antiquated, so allowed to be held in honour

indicators.note: to be held in something is to be kept inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
taken as written
let means allowed, as in let go

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned award is kept on because it has been permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British royal honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete is outdated and no longer used, just like something antiquated.

clue.text: Give up what's offered

definitions.meaning: to surrender or forgo something for a greater good
an offering made to a god, such as a slaughtered animal

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to forgo something precious; the noun is an offering made to a deity.

clue.text: The opposite of night-vision?

parts.note: night-vision suggests seeing in the dark, but here a vision at night is a dream, so its opposite is a dream by day

explanation.surface: A quiz on the opposite of military night-vision gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Night-vision sounds like the goggles soldiers wear; read it as a vision seen at night, a dream, and the daytime version is a reverie.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydream is a pleasant reverie indulged while awake, a dream had in daylight rather than in sleep.

clue.text: Light diet may be ordered

indicators.note: to be ordered is to be put in order, so the letters of diet may are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A doctor may prescribe a light diet for a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like part of 'light diet', but it is the definition; 'be ordered' rearranges DIET MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Daytime is the period of daylight, so the answer is a noun for light as opposed to dark.

clue.text: Municipal palindrome

indicators.note: a palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards, which this five-letter word does

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A one-word description of a town hall that reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic means relating to a city or town and its government, the same as municipal.

clue.text: Energy coming out of volcano in Asian land

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as in says

parts.note: vim means energy or vigour
Etna is the active volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Geothermal energy pours out of a volcano somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out of' joins the two halves: the energy has the volcano inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a country in South-East Asia, bordering China, Laos and Cambodia.

clue.text: Extremely nervous?

parts.note: a person who is extremely nervous is on edge, and the word also hints at being at the edges or extremes

explanation.surface: A one-line question about someone very jumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks you to take extremes as edges: someone right at the edge is nervy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge means jumpy and tense, so the adjective describes a very nervous, anxious person.

clue.text: Private communication of faith

definitions.meaning: a secret told to someone in trust
trust or belief in someone or something

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a secret shared in trust, and also firm trust or belief in someone.

clue.text: Head of choir soon becomes a priest

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from choir

parts.note: anon is an old word meaning soon or shortly

explanation.surface: The choirmaster will shortly be ordained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral, one of its chapter of priests.

clue.text: Old punishment governor included for offending pupil

indicators.note: included means taken inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails was a whip used for flogging in the past
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: In the old days a school governor approved of the cane for a misbehaving child.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'cat' is the cat-o'-nine-tails whip; HE is His Excellency, how a governor is addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat is someone who breaks the rules dishonestly, such as a pupil copying in an exam.

clue.text: Article on foreign currency includes one no longer current

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the cent is a coin of the US and the eurozone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A foreign coin, with a note attached, turns out to be one that has been withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like money, picking up 'currency', but here means present-day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancient is very old, belonging to times long past rather than the present day.

clue.text: She has promised to give a hand

definitions.text: She has promised to give a hand

parts.words: She has promised to give a hand
parts.note: to give someone your hand is to agree to marry them, not just to help out

explanation.surface: A woman has pledged to help someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give a hand' looks like helping out, but a hand given in marriage is the sense meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancee is a woman engaged to be married, one who has promised her hand in marriage.

clue.text: Chaperon is expected to bring the girl back

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due

indicators.note: back means the word for the girl is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An escort is due to take the young lady home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ANN, giving NNA; 'to bring' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who acts as a chaperon to girls in a Spanish or Portuguese family.

clue.text: Wood used in the new case for personal protection

indicators.note: used in means put to work inside, so one piece goes inside the other
new means made afresh, so the letters of the word the are rearranged

parts.note: elm is a hardwood timber tree

explanation.surface: A wooden box made for someone's protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges THE into HET. 'case' looks like wordplay for a container, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet encases the head, a protective covering worn by soldiers, riders and builders.
